question: The inputs are unquantified paired-end FASTQ files (6 samples, 3 treated vs 3 control, human liver), but this environment has no way to turn reads into counts. Can you either (a) provide a gene-level count matrix (or transcript abundance files) for these 6 samples, or (b) have a transcriptome/genome index plus an aligner or pseudoaligner provisioned? Without one of these, no differential-expression plan can actually run.

input.questionContext:
What I checked before asking:

1. Quantification tooling — no read-level tool is installed in the sandbox and nothing can be installed at run time. Absent: salmon, kallisto, STAR, HISAT2, bowtie2, RSEM, subread/featureCounts, fastp, cutadapt, trim-galore, fastqc, multiqc, samtools, seqkit, kb-python. The CLI package track is empty entirely. On the R side, Rsubread, Rbowtie2, Rhisat2 and QuasR are all absent; only downstream/IO packages exist (Rsamtools, ShortRead, Biostrings, GenomicAlignments, GenomicFeatures). ShortRead can read FASTQ but cannot align or pseudoalign, so it cannot produce counts.

2. Reference sequence — /mnt/refs holds the GENCODE v50 human GTF (annotation only, no sequence), hg38 chrom sizes, liftOver chains, blacklists, MSigDB/Reactome/WikiPathways GMTs, STRING, CollecTRI/DoRothEA/PROGENy, GTEx v8, LINCS, and a PharmCAT GRCh38 FASTA tarball. There is no transcriptome FASTA and no prebuilt salmon/kallisto/STAR index. The BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38 R package is present, so a transcript FASTA could in principle be extracted — but there is still no aligner to use it with, and building an index from scratch for 6 samples is not viable here.

3. Networking — the sandbox has no network access, so a script cannot fetch an index or reference at run time.

Everything downstream of a count matrix is fully supported (DESeq2 1.52.0, edgeR, limma, pydeseq2, apeglm/ashr, EnhancedVolcano, fgsea/clusterProfiler, plus human hallmark/GO/Reactome/WikiPathways gene sets for follow-up enrichment), so as soon as counts exist the treated-vs-control analysis is straightforward. The gap is strictly the FASTQ-to-counts step.
